name: p0-review-guard-v1
hypothesis: Capability dismissals follow weak half-year reviews that the run itself announces (C/D grades, feedback that the next review must be better), and P0 shows no corrective shift after them. A single feedback-triggered review-recovery mode (visible-delivery main actions, Prepare report materials, wellbeing guard) with an explicit exit on a B-or-better review converts the next review into a solid grade, removing review-driven eliminations without costing the trust/risk or wellbeing behaviour that lets P0 complete runs.
change: P0 text unchanged in steps 1-5; description mentions the mode; adds one 'Review recovery' section: trigger = C/D grade or feedback that performance fell short or must improve; while active, main action Report results to your manager or Showcase results, Energy on Prepare report materials first with Health/Mental recovery taking precedence when Health or Dignity is low or falling, story options that finish work and make real results visible; notes start with 'recovery'; exit = a later review graded B or better.
predicted_behaviour: After the first C or D, the next two quarterly phases show Report results to your manager or Showcase results as main action and Prepare report materials in Energy far more often than in P0 on the same seeds; notes start with 'recovery' from the trigger until the next B-or-better review, then stop; the review after a C is more often B or better than in P0; fewer eliminations of the weak-review/capability direction; Health and Dignity at the trigger+2 quarters no lower than P0; no rise in trust/risk eliminations; token cost per month only slightly above P0.
refutation: Refuted if, on paired runs against P0, the share of reviews after a C/D that are B or better does not rise, or capability-direction eliminations do not fall. Refuted as harmful if completion rate or mean quantitative_score drops, or Health/Dignity-direction or trust-crisis eliminations rise. Execution failure (not a test of the idea) if fewer than half of post-C/D quarterly phases contain the recovery main action or the 'recovery' note label, or if the label persists after a B-or-better review (missing exit, P08).
notes: Minimal child of P0 (the best observed policy so far). The trigger is the run's own published feedback (grade letters and their public meanings), not a hidden threshold; 'repeated weak reviews can end the run' paraphrases the public failure direction 'repeated low performance'. No calendar trigger: the mode is entered and left only on review feedback. Recovery deliberately avoids High-intensity work so Output is bought with Prepare report materials and report/showcase actions, which also raise Dignity. The note label makes mode dwell time measurable from logs (P02 fold-in check).
